finding.claim: DELETE /accounts/{id} performs no authorization: the result of canDelete(u, a) is discarded, so any authenticated user can delete any existing account.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled path parameter `id` (line 20) with any authenticated `User u`. Precondition: caller reaches this method with a valid session (not visible in this repo).
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at line 23, a protected state-changing operation.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) receives attacker-chosen id.
a = accounts.get(id) loads any account regardless of owner.
canDelete(u, a) evaluated but boolean result ignored; no throw or branch.

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is logically correct (admin or owner) but never enforced in deleteAccount. assertCanDelete (13-17) is not called here, unlike closeAccount (line 29). No ownership check precedes removal. Upstream callers/filters are not in the repo, so an upstream check cannot be fully ruled out, but none is visible.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) returns a bool, but deleteAccount discards it as a bare statement at line 22, so nothing is enforced. assertCanDelete (13-17) would throw, but it is not called in deleteAccount (it is only used in closeAccount at line 29). No other check exists in the repo before accounts.remove(id) at line 23.
verdict.reason: At AccountService.java:22 the canDelete(u, a) result is discarded, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any caller who passes the upstream auth check; the only file in the repo is this one, so no upstream authorization check is visible to block it.

finding.claim: Non-admin requests for a nonexistent id throw NullPointerException instead of a denial or not-found response, creating an existence oracle for account ids.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled `id` (line 20) for a non-existent account, with a non-admin `User u`.
finding.sink: Dereference of a.ownerId() at line 10, reached via canDelete(u, a) at line 22 with a == null.

trace.note: accounts.get(id) returns null for unknown id.
u.admin() false for non-admins, so a.ownerId() on null throws NPE.

finding.guards_checked: No null check on `a` before canDelete at line 22. Same NPE path exists in closeAccount via assertCanDelete (lines 28-29). Admins unaffected because u.admin() short-circuits. Low severity; meaningful mainly when combined with AS-1 or when error responses reach the client.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) returns a bool, but deleteAccount calls it as a bare statement at line 22 and ignores the result, so the call only matters for its NPE. The throwing guard assertCanDelete (lines 13-17) is used only in closeAccount, not deleteAccount. Admin short-circuit at line 10 is the only thing that avoids the NPE.
verdict.reason: For a non-admin user, deleteAccount(u, id) with an unknown id reaches a.ownerId() on null at AccountService.java:10 via the discarded call at line 22, so it throws NullPointerException, while an existing id returns normally, which gives an existence oracle; the same discarded-result bug at line 22 also lets any authenticated user delete accounts they don't own, which the candidate did not report.
